data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Aviation checklists are often used by experts, whereas the prompt specifies non-experts."],"overturn_conditions":["Evidence that checklists in high-stakes environments increase error rates due to cognitive overload."],"shared_structure":["High-skill individual (Surgeon/Pilot) vs. Systematic safety protocol","Prevention of 'stupid' mistakes vs. Enhancement of peak skill"],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_004"],"transfer_claims":["The 'Surgical Safety Checklist' model demonstrates that reliability gains come from raising the floor rather than raising the ceiling."]},"claim":"A panel of non-experts using a checklist is more reliable on average because it replaces the high-variance 'peak' performance of an expert with a high-floor 'baseline' performance, effectively filtering out catastrophic idiosyncratic errors.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires synthesis of non-linear variables that cannot be decomposed into a checklist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is so granular that it induces 'compliance fatigue' (per SCR_005), leading to missed checks.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's 'intuition' is actually a high-speed processing of the same checklist items, but with superior weighting.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Variance reduction via systematic decomposition: The checklist acts as a low-pass filter (per SCR_002) that removes high-frequency noise (random expert slips) while ensuring that the minimum required criteria for a correct outcome are met, shifting the mean reliability upward even if the maximum possible 'insight' is lowered.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
